title: MP Materials' 10X Financing: Cash, Covenants, and Construction Risk
cover_lines: How a lapsed JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs commitment gave way to equity and a JPMorgan-agented revolver
Benjamin Yang · Research draft 1.0 candidate · 11 November 2026 · Evidence to 6 November 2026
Independent research; not commissioned or reviewed by JPMorgan or MP Materials. Pending human review; publication hold remains in place.

exhibit.title: An actual suspension of a Defense payment obligation blocks revolver draws at once; lenders may act after 60 or 90 days
exhibit.subtitle: Revolver states under credit agreement Section 8.01(m); no such event is reported
exhibit.annotation: Plain reading of the filed agreement, not legal advice. The clock starts when an obligation is actually suspended or released; a mere right to suspend is arguably not a Default. Restoring it in time avoids an Event of Default. A late DoD payment is not clearly a trigger. Remedies need lender action.

exhibit.title: Leverage tests start by Q3 2027, before expected 2028 10X commissioning, and the 2030 notes can pull maturity into 2029
exhibit.subtitle: Reported dates, contract deadlines and one conditional date; none is an MP plan
exhibit.annotation: Trigger: earlier at $400m of covenant EBITDA, later only on a late filing. On $1,043.1m of debt, 4.00x leverage needs about $232m ($209m with 100% netting); 3.00x coverage, at most $108–109m. If enough 2030 notes remain, maturity springs unless cash plus availability tops $1,078.5m or leverage is 2.00x or less.
exhibit.source: Credit agreement §§1.01, 6.01(b), 7.11; Q3 2026 10-Q, Note 8 and MD&A

exhibit.title: The Defense agreements that support MP are also revolver default triggers
exhibit.subtitle: Government instruments linked to MP Materials; the transaction, offtake and price protection agreements are named in the credit agreement
exhibit.annotation: Support narrows named price and volume risks; construction cost, timing and financing stay with MP. DoD may suspend offtake performance only after an uncured MP payment default; the filed price agreement has no suspension right. A material 10X breach left uncured past cure and notice periods lets DoD terminate, a revolver Event of Default.
exhibit.source: Transaction agreement §§6.13, 9.02(a); offtake §8.4; price protection §8(p)–(q); credit agreement §8.01(m); 2025 10-K, Note 3

data.relationship: Declared government links; spokes carry no value.

slides.label: Strongest alternative

exhibit.title: The revolver helps in a fundable overrun; a suspension of Defense payments blocks it
exhibit.subtitle: Both options raise the same $724.2m of equity at the same dilution; they differ in what happens under stress
exhibit.annotation: Editorial judgment, draft 1.0 candidate, 11 November 2026; pending human review. Before the covenant trigger a draw adds cash toward the $500m quarter-end floor; after it, a draw raises leverage. Equity only is better if covenant EBITDA would fall short of about $232m at the first leverage test.
exhibit.source: FI003 analysis; credit agreement; transaction agreement §9.02(a); 2025 10-K; Q3 2026 10-Q

exhibit.title: Four conditions test whether equity plus a revolver still holds; each failure points to another path
exhibit.subtitle: Decision conditions for a hypothetical sponsor; the highlighted route ends at the recommendation
exhibit.annotation: Editorial judgment, draft 1.0 candidate, 11 November 2026; pending human review. Go and slow decisions on 10X are set on projected quarter-end cash of at least $500m, then covenant EBITDA of at least about $232m ($209m on the 100% reading); revolver capacity is a secondary buffer. A sponsor without an anchor offtake or price floor may lack the equity window.
exhibit.source: FI003 analysis; credit agreement; transaction agreement
